page: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the Cost Optimized family, provisioned via the QEMU hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by 4 shared AMD EPYC virtual cores running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores at 1 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU, and bundles 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance does not include a GPU and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the cx33 in the middle tier for baseline processing and memory bandwidth, reaching a stress-ng single-core score of 2672.38 and multi-core score of 10641.52. PassMark testing reports an overall CPU score of 8691.84 and a database operations score of 3447.6. However, heavy multi-threaded compute reflects shared CPU limits, as seen in a Geekbench multi-core score of 4356.0 and a Clang software compilation score of 5229.0. Memory bandwidth measures 470.59 GB/sec for small cached reads, 67.66 GB/sec for uncached large reads, and 49.67 GB/sec for uncached writes. The server handles 7.84 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers 6.15 GB/sec in static web serving.

The primary tradeoff of the cx33 is its shared CPU allocation model, which trades strict execution consistency for high resource cost efficiency. Bundled NVMe storage ensures fast local read and write operations, but the 8.0 GB memory footprint limits heavy concurrent processing. The instance is technically suited for development environments, lightweight web hosting, background job workers, small Redis caching instances, and low-traffic database backends.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is a cost-optimized virtual server configured with 4 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs at 2.0 GHz, 8.0 GB of system memory, and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage on x86_64 architecture. Designed for budget-oriented deployments without hardware accelerators, it offers an economical 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Benchmark results show dependable baseline performance, recording a PassMark CPU score of 8691.84, a multi-core stress-ng result of 10641.52, and 7.84 million Redis SET operations per second. However, sustained parallel workloads like Clang compilation reveal shared-resource limits. The server is well suited for dev/test clusters, lightweight web serving, and small background tasks.
